--- title: "[BuckleyJames]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Buckley-James rank-based accelerated failure time regression. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_buckley_james.py#L105-L434){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python BuckleyJames( *, max_iter=200, tol=1e-06, n_boot=None, seed=None, conf_level=0.95 ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Fits $\log(T) = X\beta + \varepsilon$ without assuming a distribution for $\varepsilon$, by alternating Kaplan-Meier-based imputation of censored log-times with ordinary least squares refitting until $\beta$ stabilizes. This is a semiparametric alternative to `AFT`: it avoids committing to a parametric error distribution, at the cost of an iterative fit, occasional slow or oscillating convergence, and no closed-form standard errors (available here only via optional bootstrap resampling, `n_boot=`). When there is no censoring at all, every residual is exact and the algorithm converges in a single step to the ordinary least squares fit of $\log(T)$ on $X$. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[200]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of Buckley-James iterations (default `200`). [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance on the largest change in any coefficient between iterations (default `1e-6`). [n_boot]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of bootstrap resamples for standard errors and confidence intervals. If `None` (the default), `std_error_`, `conf_low_`, and `conf_high_` are `nan` (Buckley-James has no closed-form variance). [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for bootstrap resampling (ignored if `n_boot` is `None`). [conf_level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level for bootstrap coefficient intervals (default `0.95`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Fitted estimator]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Call `fit()` to produce a fitted estimator with cached results (`coef_`, `std_error_`, `z_`, `p_value_`, `conf_low_`, `conf_high_`, `n_iter_`, `converged_`, `loglik_`-free since there is no likelihood), accessible as arrays or exported to DataFrames. ::: ## Details {.doc-details} Call `fit(surv, covariates)` with a right-censored `Surv` response and a covariate design (a 2-D array, a dataframe, or a formula string with `data`). An intercept is added automatically. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#f2cce787 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and build a right-censored response lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") y = gw.Surv.right(lung["time"], event=(lung["status"] == 2)) # Fit a Buckley-James model bj = gw.BuckleyJames().fit(y, lung[["age", "sex"]]) bj ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` BuckleyJames (rank-based accelerated failure time regression) coef se(coef) z p (Intercept) 6.379 NA NA NA age -0.02306 NA NA NA sex 0.4912 NA NA NA n = 228, events = 165 iterations = 13, converged = True ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
fit() Fit the Buckley-James model to survival data.
predict() Predict the linear predictor or survival probabilities from the fitted model.
to_frame() Return the coefficient table as a DataFrame.
### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the Buckley-James model to survival data. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_buckley_james.py#L205-L319){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(surv, covariates, *, data=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A right-censored `Surv` response. Built with `Surv.right()`. [covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A dataframe (pandas or polars), a 2-D array, or a formula string (e.g., `"age + sex"`) evaluated against the `data` argument. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A dataframe to evaluate the formula string (ignored if `covariates` is a dataframe or array). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [BuckleyJames]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The fitted estimator itself (for method chaining) with cached coefficient arrays (`coef_`, `std_error_`, `z_`, `p_value_`) and convergence diagnostics (`n_iter_`, `converged_`). ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#d13c2a3b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") y = gw.Surv.right(lung["time"], event=(lung["status"] == 2)) bj = gw.BuckleyJames().fit(y, lung[["age", "sex"]]) bj ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` BuckleyJames (rank-based accelerated failure time regression) coef se(coef) z p (Intercept) 6.379 NA NA NA age -0.02306 NA NA NA sex 0.4912 NA NA NA n = 228, events = 165 iterations = 13, converged = True ``` ::: ::: ### [predict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict the linear predictor or survival probabilities from the fitted model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_buckley_james.py#L327-L393){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict(newdata=None, *, type="survival", times=None, format=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [newdata]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Covariate values for prediction. A DataFrame (Pandas or Polars), 2-D array, or `None` (the default, uses the training data). [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["survival"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : `"survival"` (default): survival probabilities $S(t \mid x)$ at `times`, evaluated by shifting the fitted residual Kaplan-Meier curve by each subject's linear predictor. `"lp"`: the linear predictor $X\beta$ (log-time location) only; returns an array. [times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Query times for `type="survival"` (ignored for `"lp"`). Required for `"survival"`. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format for `type="survival"`: `None` (auto-detect), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. Ignored for `type="lp"` (which always returns an array). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ndarray or DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : An array of shape `(n_subjects,)` for `type="lp"`. A DataFrame with a `time` column and one column per subject for `type="survival"`. ::: #### Details {.doc-details} Because Buckley-James makes no distributional assumption, survival predictions reuse the empirical Kaplan-Meier curve of the fitted residuals rather than a closed-form survival function: $S(t \mid x) = \hat{S}_{\text{resid}}(\log t - x^\top\hat\beta)$. This curve is only as reliable as the residual sample size and is not smooth like `AFT`'s or `RoystonParmar`'s predictions. #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#5cb6840c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") y = gw.Surv.right(lung["time"], event=(lung["status"] == 2)) bj = gw.BuckleyJames().fit(y, lung[["age", "sex"]]) bj.predict(lung[["age", "sex"]][:2], type="survival", times=[180, 365, 730], format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
